title: Tectum Panels
short_answer: Cementitious wood-fiber acoustic panel. Genuinely easy to install and genuinely easy to wreck — almost every defect is a crushed edge or an over-driven screw.
summary: Cementitious wood-fiber acoustic panel. Genuinely easy to install and genuinely easy to wreck — almost every defect is a crushed edge or an over-driven screw.
plain_words: Tectum is a stiff panel made of wood shreds held together with cement. It absorbs sound and takes a beating, so it goes in gyms, corridors, pools and mechanical rooms. It screws straight to framing or furring. Two rules do most of the work: screw heads flush with the face — never countersunk, and do not bang the corners, because a crushed corner cannot be repaired.
when_to_use: Direct-attach Tectum ceiling or wall panels per the submittal
Gyms, corridors, pools, and mechanical rooms where lay-in ACT is wrong
After substrate / furring is flat and the layout is planned
prerequisites: Approved submittal for the specified Tectum product line
Flat furring or structure — string and shim before panels go up
Dust control plan for abrasive cutting

tools.name: Screw gun with clutch set from scrap test
Laser or string line for layout

materials.name: Tectum direct-attach panel (per submittal thickness and size)
Screws or nails per substrate and submittal

steps.title: Confirm product and substrate
steps.body: Aspen fiber with cementitious binder — abrasive to cut, holds screws well. Direct-attach goes to structure or furring, not lay-in grid. Standard direct-attach is often 1" thick in 2×4', 2×8', and 4×8' — check the submittal for other lines.

steps.title: Flat substrate
steps.body: String furring and shim before start — Tectum will not bridge a wavy wall or out-of-plane furring run.

steps.title: Layout
steps.body: Plan joints like a ceiling: border pieces large and even, no sliver borders. Same principle as Acoustical Ceilings layout.

steps.title: Fasteners and spacing
steps.body: Screws, nails, or adhesive per submittal. Screw-head pull-through is adequate — no washers or adhesive required alongside screws. Minimum 24" o.c. from panel edge; 12" o.c. on furring. Fastener must account for total system weight.

steps.title: Never countersink
steps.body: Screw heads flush with the face — never countersunk, never proud. Set clutch on scrap first; crushed fiber around the head cannot be filled away.

steps.title: Cutting and handling
steps.body: Carbide blade; dusty and abrasive — cut outside finished space when possible. Carry on edge; corners crush easily — replace, do not patch.

steps.title: Joints and finish
steps.body: Keep joints tight and aligned. If field painted, follow manufacturer method — heavy rolled paint fills texture and kills acoustic performance.

steps.title: Fastener spacing verified
steps.body: Per submittal, starting at panel edges.

steps.title: Layout and edges
steps.body: Joints tight and aligned; layout even, no sliver borders. No crushed corners — replace damaged panels.

steps.title: Cut edges and faces
steps.body: Cut edges treated per submittal. Panel faces clean — texture not clogged with paint or dust.

warnings.title: Countersinking
warnings.body: Driving screw heads in crushes fiber, leaves a dark dimple, and there is no filler that makes it disappear — the texture is the finish.

warnings.title: Field paint
warnings.body: Heavy rolled paint fills the texture and kills the acoustic performance — the entire reason the panel is there.

warnings.title: Scope question for GVC
warnings.body: Tectum is a title-only stub in the portal estimate scope catalog. Before pricing, confirm: furnish or install-only; who owns furring and substrate prep; whether field painting is ours.

experts.summary: Fasteners: screws, nails, or adhesive per substrate and submittal. Pull-through of screw heads is adequate alone — no washers or adhesive alongside screws. Minimum 24" o.c. from panel edge; 12" o.c. on furring. Fastener selection must account for total system weight. Do not countersink — heads flush with face. Do not let substrate telegraph — string and shim furring like Z-furring work. Cutting: carbide blade; dusty/abrasive — eye protection and dust control. Cut edges are visible — plan layout so cuts land where least seen. Corners crush — carry on edge, stack flat. Layout like ACT: even borders, no slivers. Field paint per manufacturer — heavy paint kills acoustics.

variations.title: Wall direct-attach
changes: Gravity and handling make corner crush more likely — carry on edge

variations.title: Ceiling direct-attach
changes: Fastener must account for total system weight including overhead load
Layout borders matter from every sight line in the room

quality_checks.prompt: Every screw head flush — none countersunk, none proud
Fastener spacing per submittal from panel edges
No crushed corners or edges — damaged panels replaced
Layout even with no sliver borders

common_mistakes.title: Countersunk screws
common_mistakes.wrong: Drive heads below the face to "hide" fasteners
common_mistakes.right: Flush heads only — set clutch on scrap
common_mistakes.why: Crushed fiber and dark dimples are permanent on a texture finish

common_mistakes.title: Wavy substrate
common_mistakes.right: String and shim furring before the first panel

common_mistakes.title: Crushed corners
common_mistakes.wrong: Lean panels against walls or drag corners
common_mistakes.right: Carry on edge; replace crushed panels

common_mistakes.title: Heavy field paint
common_mistakes.wrong: Roll paint like standard gypsum board
common_mistakes.right: Follow manufacturer method; light application only if specified

troubleshooting.fix: Replace affected panels; reset clutch on scrap before continuing

troubleshooting.likely_cause: Substrate not flat or furring out of plane
troubleshooting.fix: Stop; shim furring and re-string before more panels go up
